program: Low-vision support, assistive technology and employment training
priceScope: Conditional annual whole-recipient cost divided by a limited modeled local channel; not a verified marginal gift offer or complete portfolio EV

what: The Lighthouse of Houston provides low-vision health services, assistive technology, training and community programs.
It also offers employment through business services and supports independent living.
The deep review uses separate low-vision and training contact envelopes, full consolidated annual costs, and signed health plus net household resources.
strengths: A randomized low-vision rehabilitation trial supports functional improvement beyond basic care, although it does not measure Houston QALYs.
Current course descriptions identify training content, fees and public workforce referral alternatives.
Consolidated audited accounts make it possible to avoid counting related-entity transfers twice.
reservations: The report chart gives 500 clinic and 411 training contacts, not unique clients or incremental placements.
Current employment shares do not establish additional jobs or earnings caused by donations.
Whole consolidated cost versus the narrow modeled channel is not complete portfolio EV or a marginal gift estimate.

sections.what: The Lighthouse of Houston provides low-vision health services, assistive technology, training and community programs. It also offers employment through business services and supports independent living. The deep review uses separate low-vision and training contact envelopes, full consolidated annual costs, and signed health plus net household resources.
sections.monitoring: The 2025 annual report chart records 500 low-vision clinic and 411 technology education/training contacts within 24,084 mixed impacts; neither chart nor total is a deduplicated outcome cohort. Its employee statement explicitly refers to 2024. Ask for dated unique clients, completed certifications, referral funding, retained after-tax earnings and comparison outcomes. Contact counts, employees and certification launch do not establish additional jobs.
sections.qualitative: LOVIT II randomized 323 predominantly elderly male veterans to rehabilitation or basic low-vision care. Four-month functional improvements support a mechanism, while the generic health measure did not differ; Houston utility gain, clinical response and persistence remain judgments. Device-only, insurance, workforce referral and other training providers remain alternatives. Operating EIN 74-1146781 differs from Foundation 74-1618607; the consolidated boundary includes living centers and removes internal grants and management fees once.
sections.cost: The conditional annual two-channel estimate changes from $9.81M to $38.94M per better life: 1.872733 health QALYs and -0.023191 signed income equivalents. This is mainly a cohort and burden-accounting revision, not evidence the whole organization became four times less effective. The old-cohort burden-only case isolates accounting from the narrower current reference. Full FY2025 consolidated annual cost remains $7,201,649. N=911 is the chart contact envelope (500 clinic plus 411 training), not unique people; unique=.8 and Houston share=.95 are judgments. Clinical responders equal 500 × .8 × .5 additionality × .4 response; utility .015 for two years and half-year delay remain hypotheses, not trial QALYs. Resource successes are 411 × .8 × .5 × .15; only this training subgroup can receive $4,000 disposable earnings after tax, benefits withdrawal and recurring work costs. Joint $100 otherwise-paid care saving is a conservative hypothesis limited to that same household subgroup, not a separate duplicated population. Positive components alone retain .75 overlap; every exposed household incurs $100 access burden and .0005 QALY harm, even if b=0. One joint log per household uses $25,000 annual consumption. Central assumes funded training but not free public resources: payer and training-time effects are unresolved and tested separately. Full self-pay sensitivity charges $2,495 tuition plus 150 hours at judged $15/hour only to the training subgroup, in addition to access cost. Partial certification, short health persistence, clinical null, lost work, displaced workers and payer/provider losses are explicit scenarios. Payer losses allocate Houston recipients once then apply editionShare=1. A no-exposure case is distinct from ineffective existing services with burdens. All other programs remain unmeasured, not zero; full organization cost against two partial benefit channels is neither total portfolio EV nor verified next-gift capacity.
sections.funding: Official donations support the operating charity. Current course fees and TWC referral routes establish funding alternatives, not a charitable marginal placement price. Public or employer costs and displaced-worker losses require evidence before asserting complete net welfare.

model.costScope: Full consolidated FY2025 expenses including merchandise costs and direct donor benefits, net of internal transfers, versus a partial health and training channel.
model.geographicAttribution: Greater Houston services with judged local share 0.95; consolidated living-center coverage may differ.
model.formula: exposed=N*unique; clinical responders=clinicalN*unique*b*clinicalResponse; health=(responders*q*discounted T - exposed*harm)*g; training successes=trainingN*unique*b*success; joint signed household log gains and full all-exposure burdens; local payer allocations once; price=10*C/(health+income-equivalent)
model.counterfactual: Basic low-vision care, public workforce and insurance funding, other training providers, and ordinary earnings retained. Trial effects cannot be imported as Houston utility or placement estimates.
model.attribution: Additional benefits apply to b responders; all service exposure burdens and harm remain full. Training earnings only for its own subgroup.
model.uncertainty: Unresolved unique clients, Houston share, placement response, generic utility, persistence, payer costs and gift capacity; source-scope change separated from accounting correction.
model.nativeOutcomes: 2025 report chart: 500 low-vision clinic and 411 training contacts; 24,084 mixed impacts are not unique clients or successful placements.
